edit_summary: Two commits. (1) 12fd1241c5cc625677118d80efbfc6ecc74dc294 - documents only - closes round 1's Critical AND all ten findings from a cross-model whole-package audit. Round 1's Critical, found independently by both reviewers: REQ-003's advisory/required byte-identity guarantee was unsatisfiable on the Full track, because its permitted-difference set was three fields inside Resolver Evidence while its own parenthetical says those digests hash the canonical Project Context and Context Projection texts - and generated/project-context.resolved.json IS that Projection, so its bytes must differ, and facet-manifest.yaml fails identically via its own context_binding. The exception is now stated as enforcement-derived fields excepted WHEREVER THEY OCCUR: Resolver Evidence's state; full_context_revision and projection_sha256 in every artifact whose schema carries them; and, in the Projection, its workflow block and source_sha256. Both reviewers note that scope is derivable from investigation.md INV-004's own schema field lists rather than a new decision, and the Lite track is untouched since capability-summary.yaml carries no context_binding. Five sites: REQ-003 prose, AC-016, TEST-016, and three in design.md including a verbatim quote of the TEST-016 row that would otherwise have gone stale. (2) The same commit closes ten findings from an exhaustive Codex audit over all seven frozen documents, run because the spec stage's reviewers may read only requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md and eight attempts had each surfaced a different pre-existing defect. FIVE of the ten are in files no spec-stage reviewer can read. Four were spot-verified against live bytes before any edit. Closed: requirements.md said the Resolver 'reads the clock, the network, and no provider API', the exact inverse of the guarantee its own next clause quotes - corrected to 'reads neither the clock nor the network'; the ruling-D(2) sweep had inserted a Block-record clause into the RECOVERABLE MIX branch, which raises no Block and proceeds into a fresh resolve, against AC-047 - that branch now restores every journal member including Evidence and writes no Block record, in design.md and infra-spec.md, with the direct Evidence record reserved to the unrecoverable branch; the diagnostic-row partitions summed to seventeen in traceability.md and nineteen in tasks.md, and the two disagreed with each other - counting each task's own id list gives 5+5+3+3=16, the surplus being extra snapshot-generation-mismatch FIXTURES counted as rows; AC-026 required 'all ten' suites while tasks.md and traceability.md say nine and defer the tenth - narrowed to the nine scheduled, the alternative being a tasks.md scope expansion not the orchestrator's to take; the pre-publication ordering absolute, impossible for the two transaction-phase Blocks; the security authorization table's 'never a bare direct write', which forbade the very path REQ-001/REQ-004/design.md mandate and the only path the unrecoverable-journal Block can take; the PRE/POST convergence absolutes in security-spec and infra-spec against the unrecoverable branch's deliberate mixed state; 'the one exception' naming only post-publication-generation-mismatch and omitting artifact-publication-failed; and 'No assembly step branches on capability_enforcement' against step 10b, which does. Seven files touched; no AC or TEST id added, renumbered or removed; the enum stays closed at sixteen; no exception added to REQ-002; traceability.md's Status column untouched. Commit a9a5d3377cad99439831c1b2d077cfe0cf6a9aa1 records all of it in investigation.md with per-document SHA-256 for all seven.
